editorialRead.headline: Morning Read — October 22, 2026
editorialRead.readHeadline: pydantic/pydantic-ai is the first source to inspect.
editorialRead.oneLineSummary: pydantic/pydantic-ai leads a 3-item attention queue backed by direct receipts; 30 watchlist sources are fresh, 0 need source-health attention, and movement still requires editorial judgment.
editorialRead.dek: Agent Pulse filtered 30 included projects down to 3 items worth finite newsroom attention. The queue protects attention; it does not declare winners.
bullets: pydantic/pydantic-ai — 37 commits today, 0.7 above its current daily pace, with 23 hardening-subject points. Inspect the receipt before assigning a story.
openclaw/openclaw — 603 commits landed today. Keep it on watch, but require the next receipt to prove a reader consequence before promoting it.
browser-use/browser-use — No same-day commit after 72 commits in the seven-day window. The pause is notable enough to preserve, not enough to turn into a story.
editorialRead.watchNext: The next meaningful upgrade is feedback flow: issues opened and closed, review latency, stale backlog, and the share of work that starts outside the maintainer team.
editorialRead.caveat: Source-code motion and article coverage are collected. GitHub issue flow, PR review timing, community discussion, and private backlog signals are not.

dailyInsight.headline: Pi v1.4.0 adds image inputs to more classifier routes
dailyInsight.insight: Pi v1.4.0 expands image-bearing classifier requests across provider routes. This extends earlier image support: the practical change is more ways to give a classifier the visual input itself, with distinct transport and model requirements.
dailyInsight.mechanism: Image transport differs: TypeSafe uses assets and an experimental header, Clef uses data URLs, and OpenRouter uses image_url content. Model capability declarations and integration version ranges are separate requirements.
dailyInsight.whyItMatters: A released image route creates a testable option, but teams must check the complete stack before relying on it to classify screenshots or other visual inputs.

actions.audience: Teams evaluating Pi classifiers through another agent framework
actions.label: Check compatibility before an isolated image trial
actions.instruction: Inspect the integration’s Pi version range first. In a supported disposable configuration, compare known-answer images whose distinguishing feature is visual; record the provider route and model. Preserve current versions and configuration for rollback.
actions.effort: One compatibility check followed by a bounded image trial

receipts.title: Pi v1.4.0
receipts.supports: Containing release published at 22:49 UTC, October 22 in Paris; image routes extend prior support.

receipts.title: Classifier route requirements
receipts.supports: Provider-specific transport and model requirements; some routes remain text-only.

receipts.title: Image classifier live-test definitions
receipts.supports: Known red/blue image fixtures and credential-dependent provider cases; inspected, not independently run.

confidence.basis: Pinned release containment, route code, documentation and live-test definitions inspected. Live model tests were not run. Separate integration pins remain a deployment check.

dailyInsight.limitation: This is not Pi’s first image support. Routes differ, Pi’s Vercel AI Gateway and OpenCode Jev routes remain text-only, and no live model accuracy, cost or latency comparison was performed.
dailyInsight.falsifier: A containing release cannot transport the documented images under its stated provider and model configuration.
dailyInsight.watchNext: A fixed visual task reporting correct outcomes across the chosen provider routes, with supported integration versions recorded.
